query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying an anti-oxidation coating to the equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy will improve its high-temperature resistance without sacrificing its mechanical performance.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy in the cast state
generation.mechanism: The anti-oxidation coating will prevent or reduce the oxidation of the alloy, thereby maintaining its mechanical properties at high temperatures.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature resistance and maintained mechanical performance (yield strength and ductility) of the alloy.
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 1000-1200 °C, atmosphere: air, exposure time: several hours, mechanical-loading: tensile testing
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the anti-oxidation coating in improving the high-temperature resistance of the alloy is uncertain and requires experimental verification.

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of coated and uncoated HfNbTaTiZr alloy samples at high temperatures (1000-1200 °C) in air.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated alloy samples show no significant improvement in high-temperature resistance and mechanical performance compared to the uncoated samples, the hypothesis is falsified.

The equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy was chosen to analyze the effect of each constituent elemental by the subtraction method and, thus, HfMoNbTaTiZr, HfNbTaTiZr, HfMoTaTiZr, HfMoNbTiZr, HfMoNbTaZr, and HfMoNbTaTi were studied. Among these alloys, HfMoNbTaTi has the best mechanical performance, that is, 27% compressive strain at room temperature and yield strength 367 MPa at 1400 °C. HfMoNbTaTi has great potential for elevated-temperature applications. As the alloy system does not contain very expensive elements such as Re and Ru, it is cost competitive for high-temperature applications like Nb-Hf-Ti alloys in space vehicles. Further modification of composition and/or anti-oxidation coatings are still required for high-temperature applications in the air. According to the experiment results, the effects of Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr on mechanical properties of equiatomic Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys were described. For higher room-temperature strength, one should add an element which interacts frequently with the alloy, such as Mo.
